verified.entry_point: library API: MailMimeParser::parse / Message::from, Message::addAttachmentPart / addAttachmentPartFromFile, IMessagePart::getFilename / IMimePart::getHeaderParameter / IHeader::getValue, IMimePart::setFilename, Message::setSignature, and message serialisation via getStream()
sites: src/Message/Helper/MultipartHelper.php (createAndAddPartForAttachment: name=, filename=, MIME type, transfer encoding)
src/Message/UUEncodedPart.php (uuencode filename at construction and on the setter)
src/Stream/MessagePartStream.php / src/Stream/StreamFactory.php (uuencode begin-line emission, no change needed)
verified.routes: Pattern A: write path (reported), RFC-2047 decoder, RFC-2231 decoder and split continuations, re-emitted decoded protocol parameter. Pattern B: non-MIME uuencode write path, public uuencode filename setter, parsed uuencode begin-line name, caller-supplied MIME type and transfer encoding. Injected siblings: attachment rename setter, plain-value percent decode.
verified.project_tests_run: all 609 project tests pass at pinned+injection and after the reference fix (PHP 8.3, PHPUnit 9.6)

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the library has no allow/deny decision on this path; refusing a legitimate attachment fails the functional suite, and the nearest over-block is ff-overbroad.patch (functional_fail)
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: throwing on the attack value makes the message-producing security tests error, so it cannot score; the functional suite also requires legitimate calls to succeed
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected outcome is the message and its headers themselves; there is no neighbouring or proxy object to authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no external authority returns a secret or role here; there is no fail-open case

traps.shape: Pattern A base: a caller-supplied attachment name containing CR/LF is interpolated into the composed attachment headers
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported landing point, so nothing is dismissed here

traps.shape: Pattern A far site, ordering / ineffective defence: CR/LF are removed before the RFC-2047 word is decoded, so a B- or Q-encoded word reintroduces them afterwards
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the constructor already runs a CR/LF removal over the value, so a reader concludes it is handled

traps.shape: Pattern A far site, decoder semantics and shapes: RFC-2231 percent-decoding with a charset, without a charset and across split continuations, plus the decoded parameter that is re-emitted into another header
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a getter is supposed to return the true decoded text, so stripping looks like changing parser semantics; the parse path only reads messages

traps.shape: Pattern B / route where the protection never existed, sink in another module: the uuencode filename is stored and emitted verbatim into the begin line through the non-MIME write path, the public setter and a parsed begin line
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the legacy non-MIME path, the begin line is not a MIME header, and the line is written by an external stream decorator

traps.shape: Pattern B uncovered route in the same function: the caller-supplied MIME type and transfer encoding are interpolated raw into Content-Type and Content-Transfer-Encoding while only the name is normalised
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the MIME type and encoding are developer-chosen constants rather than user data, and the advisory names the filename

traps.shape: Injected sibling, write sink: a public rename setter rebuilds the disposition header with the same composed-header idiom and trusts the new name
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a plain setter, not the reported add path; raw header setting is raw by design
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer adding the missing rename API would copy the existing composed-header idiom; getFilename() exists with no setter

traps.shape: Injected sibling, parse decoder ordering: a compatibility step percent-decodes plain quoted parameter values after the token-level sanitation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: ordinary quoted values are literals; percent-decoding them is an interoperability tweak rather than decoding, and the existing decoder already strips CR/LF
traps.realistic_because: some mailers percent-encode plain parameter values; a compatibility decode added after the token-level sanitation repeats the ordering mistake the advisory fixes
